findings.title: Chunked reader discards the 2 bytes after each chunk without validating they are CRLF (malformed chunk footer accepted)
findings.evidence:
Root cause: ChunkedReader only tracks how MANY bytes remain after a chunk (self._bytes_to_discard = 2 at line 197; initialized to 0 at line 154), not WHAT they must be. In the discard branch (lines 163-170) it calls buf.maybe_extract_at_most(self._bytes_to_discard) at line 164 and unconditionally consumes/decrements those bytes at line 167 without ever comparing them to b'
'. Reachability: an attacker who controls the request body sends a Transfer-Encoding: chunked body whose chunk footer is arbitrary garbage instead of CRLF (e.g. '5
AAAAAXX2
45
...'). _connection.py selects this reader for the SEND_BODY 'chunked' framing (READERS entry line 243), so every chunk terminator routes through lines 163-170; the malformed footer is silently accepted and h11 advances by exactly 2 bytes and resumes parsing the next chunk header. Consequence: h11 accepts the same byte stream as a valid message but assigns different chunk boundaries than a co-located lenient/common-parser reverse proxy (one that reads 'until CRLF' for the footer), which is the canonical HTTP request-smuggling precondition (GHSA-vqfr-h8mv-ghfj / CVE-2025-43859). Note the precondition is narrower than remote code execution: exploitation requires a second, independently buggy HTTP parser in the path (h11 alone is only the enabler), so this is reported as the root cause rather than an end-to-end exploit. The upstream fix (h11 0.16.0, commit 114803a2) replaces the byte count with the expected literal self._bytes_to_discard = b'
' and adds a data != expected[:len(data)] check that raises LocalProtocolError('malformed chunk footer'); this file is h11 0.14.0 and contains neither.
